body: The ReferrerPolicy enum in the webappsec referrer policy spec needs `[InvalidValueDefault, MissingValueDefault]` added to it for this to be complete.

This could use ReflectEnum but the current keyword definitions are in the fetch spec. We could define the enum in HTML but then we might end up out of sync, or we need to define the enum in the fetch spec.

diff_hunk:
@@ -8896,6 +8910,32 @@ a.setAttribute('href', 'https://example.com/'); // change the content attribute extended attribute have a default value provided by the argument provided to [ReflectDefault].

+

The [ReflectEnum] extended attribute must + take an identifier. It must only be used on attributes with a type of DOMString. Additionally, it must only appear alongside [Reflect]. The provided identifier must be that of an IDL enum, + which is used to represent the known-value keywords.

+ +

To declare the value used for the invalid value default, missing value + default, and the empty value states, in IDL the [InvalidValueDefault], [MissingValueDefault], + and [EmptyValueDefault] IDL extended attributes can be used.

+ +

IDL attributes with the [ReflectEnum] extended + attribute are limited to only known values.

+ +

The [InvalidValueDefault], [MissingValueDefault] and [EmptyValueDefault] extended attributes must either take no arguments, or take a string. They must + not appear on anything other than an enum.

+ +

body:
```
4. If attributeDefinition indicates it is an [enumerated attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-microsyntaxes.html#enumerated-attribute) and the [reflected IDL attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#reflected-idl-attribute) is defined to be [limited to only known values](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#limited-to-only-known-values):

      4.1 If contentAttributeValue does not correspond to any state of attributeDefinition (e.g., it is null and there is no [missing value default](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-microsyntaxes.html#missing-value-default)), or if it is in a state of attributeDefinition with no associated keyword value, then return the empty string.
```

I guess you could change this slightly such that the lack of InvalidValueDefault etc results in the "" or null being returned?
